newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada canola crush pace likely to slacken - crusher.
newsitem.headline: Canada canola crush pace likely to slacken - crusher.

text.p: Canadian canola crushing was expected to slacken off after two consecutive weeks of firm demand unless seed prices drop further, oilseed crushers said.
Crushers used up 61,268 tonnes of canola seed in the week ended May 21 and 54,783 tonnes the week before compared to an average 45,500 tonnes in the preceding month, statistics show.

"I was surprised at the number myself but I think this states that margins improved enough that some of the eastern processors that were on soybeans did go back to canola," Canbra Foods Ltd president Larry McNamara said.
Canbra, of Lethbridge, Alberta, resumed canola crushing last week at its 1,000-tonne-a-day plant after a spring maintenance shut down, McNamara said.
Other crushers declined comment or failed to return calls.
Canada's processors can crush up to 80,000 tonnes a week.

"We've had so many weeks around 40,000 tonnes a week, running the industry at 50 percent of capacity, certainly the potential is there, it would seem that if the market was right and the margin was there that number could really pop up," Canadian Oilseed Processors Association head Bob Broeska said.
COPA is the crushing industry's association.
Canola area was forecast to rise 32 percent to 11.585 million acres from 8.8 million in 1996/97 (Aug/July), Statistics Canada said April 30.
U.S. soybean seeded acreage at 68.8 million acres, up 6.7 percent from last spring's 64.2 million acres, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said May 12.
"Things have got to come into line in the Canadian and U.S. markets. We've got this bubble based on the huge demand in North America," Broeska added.
Canola crushers won't reveal margins but profitability in recent weeks has improved under the pressure of U.S. soybeans.
Chicago Board of Trade July soybean futures dropped 7.3 percent to US$8.36 a bushel Friday from US$9.02 on May 7.
Winnipeg Commodity Exchange July canola futures fell 5.8 percent to C$402.70 a tonne Friday from C$427.50 on May 7.
"Outside Japan you have absolutely nobody else around for old crop and that's a drag on the canola market," Continental Grain Co Canada analyst Greg Kostal said.

"To have a flamboyant market you have to have active export demand, active crush and an active cash market. The only thing we've got going for us is the crush and the other two have yet to prove themselves," Kostal said.
While the July Winnipeg Commodity Exchange futures crush margin rose to +0.34 Monday from -3.08 May 8 seed value was still seen as over priced relative to the world market, trade officials said.

"We've got to get down to a C$380 number, then you'll see more crushing and exports and the other thing that would support that is if we continue to see acres will surpass the last StatsCan number of 11.6 million," Canbra's McNamara said.
Analysts expected Canadian processors to crush 2.6 to 2.75 million tonnes of canola in the 1996/97 (Aug/July) crop year. So far 2.16 million tonnes has been crushed since Aug 1, 1996.
"We need to get closer to 12.5 to 13 million acres to give some support to continuity of supply to maintain a better crush through the balance of this year," McNamara added.
((Winnipeg Reuters bureau 204 947 3548))
